slides.title: Community and Communication
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 4 English, Unit 4: Community and Communication. Unit 4 is about community and communication — the many ways people share news, ideas and help with one another. You will read about a library service that travels by cart, a young reporter called Maya, and a town meeting that opens a new community centre. You will learn words such as service, deliver, knowledge, information, discover and priority, and use them to talk and write about your own community. By the end you will share a message clearly, just as Amal does in this unit's story, “The Circular Plan”. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Talk about services and communication in your community, using new Unit 4 words.
Describe places and things using There is and There are.
State facts about your town using the present simple (“Postal workers deliver letters daily”).
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to talk about services and communication in your community, using new Unit 4 words. You will also describe places and things using There is and There are. You will also state facts about your town using the present simple (“Postal workers deliver letters daily”). Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: service, deliver, information, thought, discover, knowledge. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: The Library That Came to Us
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes The Library That Came to Us and Maya the Young Reporter. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Countable and Uncountable Nouns

slides.narration: The first language focus is Countable and Uncountable Nouns. Some nouns can be counted one by one — one book, two books, three books — and we call these countable nouns. Other nouns cannot be split into separate items, such as water, rice or information, and we call these uncountable nouns. Knowing the difference tells you whether to reach for many or for much, so your sentences stay accurate. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Speaking 1: Describe a Service in Your Community
Writing 1: Instructions: “How to Share News in My Community”
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Describe a Service in Your Community. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
